title: tools/verify_schema_baseline.py --auto-fix references renamed migration GBL-105 (now GBL-133), auto-fix always fails and loops
registered_by: WF03-gh454-20260806 (ISS-0144 fix verification, C4 self-review step)
symptom: `python tools/verify_schema_baseline.py --check-tenants --auto-fix`, when C4-style drift (orphaned public.tenant rows with storage_mode='SCHEMA' and no matching Postgres schema) is detected, attempts to re-apply migrations/GBL-105_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql -- a file that no longer exists at that name (renamed to GBL-133_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql). Auto-fix reports 'ERROR: ... GBL-105_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql not found; cannot auto-fix', then loops (observed printing the same failing re-check + retry block 5 times in a single invocation) until Postgres connections were briefly exhausted (FATAL: sorry, too many clients already) during manual reproduction while verifying GH #454 / ISS-0144's C4 fix.
root_cause_analysis:
CONFIRMED (WF03-gh458-20260806, ISSUE-FIXER Step 1). tools/verify_schema_baseline.py hardcodes the literal filename 'GBL-105_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql' at four locations: docstring line 18 (--auto-fix flag description), auto_fix() lines 156/158/166/168 (the actual lookup path + both its success/failure print messages), argparse help text line 186, and the runtime status message at line 260 ('re-applying GBL-105...'). The actual current file on disk is migrations/GBL-133_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql -- same anti-pattern class as ISS-0088/GH#337 (stale filename reference surviving a rename), just in a tool script rather than test cleanup code.

Rename provenance VERIFIED via `git diff db362fd~1 db362fd -- migrations/GBL-105_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql migrations/GBL-133_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql` (commit db362fd, PR #405, 2026-08-03): git reports this as a rename with 88% similarity (NOT the 100%/no-content-diff originally assumed by ORCH). The 12% delta is fully accounted for and benign: commit db362fd performed a mass renumbering of ~22 other GBL-0xx migrations in the SAME commit (e.g. GBL-073->GBL-112, GBL-104->GBL-132) plus 6 newly-added 11xx-prefixed files, and GBL-105_...sql's own body contains an embedded array of those sibling filenames (for its ledger-backfill loop) plus two self-referential strings (a RAISE NOTICE label and a comment excluding its own filename from the backfill) that were correctly updated in lockstep to say GBL-133 instead of GBL-105. All CREATE/ALTER/business logic in the file is byte-identical; only these renumbered string literals differ. Confirmed via repo-wide grep that no other file still expects an executable/lookup reference to GBL-105 -- the only remaining hits are historical prose (CHANGELOG.md, src/design/fix-iss0112.md, scratch/ one-off scripts) and GBL-133's own header comment (which correctly retains 'GBL-105:' as a label describing the ORIGINAL ISS-0112 bug being fixed, not a filename lookup). Conclusion: GBL-133_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql is the sole, correct, verified successor to GBL-105 -- safe to hardcode the new name, though resolving by content/purpose (e.g. glob for '*_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql') is preferable to survive any future renumbering.

Retry-loop mechanism CONFIRMED by direct code read: main() (line 171) computes `failures` from the checks, and when `failures and args.auto_fix` (line 259) it calls auto_fix() (side-effecting only; does not mutate `failures` or return a status) and then unconditionally `return main()` (line 264) with zero depth counter, zero attempt cap, and no check that auto_fix() actually succeeded. Each recursive main() call re-opens a fresh connection via `connect(args.db_url)` inside its own `with` block (line 210). Because auto_fix() fails identically every time (GBL-105 not found -> prints to stderr and returns with no side effect), the exact same `failures` list is recomputed every recursion, so the condition at line 259 is true again forever -- recursion is bounded only by Python's call-stack recursion limit, opening one new Postgres connection per level, which matches the observed 5x-loop-then-connection-exhaustion symptom during manual reproduction.
acceptance_criteria: Update tools/verify_schema_baseline.py's hardcoded filename to the current GBL-133_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql at all four sites (docstring line 18, auto_fix() lines 156/166/168, argparse help line 186, runtime message line 260), or resolve it dynamically (e.g. glob for '*_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql' under migrations_dir) rather than a literal filename, to survive future renumbering -- dynamic resolution is the preferred fix per the ISS-0088 prevention note ('a rename anywhere silently desyncs a hardcoded string with no compile-time signal').

Add a retry cap to the auto-fix loop: replace the unconditional `return main()` at line 264 with a bounded retry (e.g. a max-attempts parameter threaded through main(), defaulting to 1 extra attempt after the initial run) so a genuinely unfixable condition fails fast with a clear terminal error instead of recursing until stack/connection exhaustion. auto_fix() should also return a bool/status so the caller can distinguish 'fix applied, recheck once' from 'fix failed, stop immediately' rather than always re-invoking main() on any failure.

Verify --auto-fix actually reconciles a deliberately-orphaned tenant row in a test run (this is currently unverified -- ISS-0144's resolution notes the tool's own auto-fix path was broken and orphaned rows had to be cleaned up directly via SQL instead).

resolution_plan.designer_notes: This is a Type E fix (behavioral change to error handling + optional dynamic filename resolution, not a pure CRUD/migration/list-page/node artefact) -- route to CODE-DESIGNER for a prose design covering: (1) the filename resolution strategy (static rename to GBL-133 vs. dynamic glob -- recommend dynamic glob on '*_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql' as it is strictly more future-proof and the ISS-0088 precedent explicitly recommends avoiding hardcoded literals that silently desync on rename), (2) the auto_fix()/main() control-flow change to cap retries (recommend: extract the check-and-report logic out of main() into a run_checks() helper returning `failures`, so main() can loop up to N times calling run_checks() -> auto_fix() -> run_checks() without recursive stack growth, OR simplest minimal fix: add a `depth: int = 0` parameter to main() with `if depth >= 1: return 1` guard before recursing), (3) BACKEND-DEV must verify the fix with a real drift scenario per acceptance criterion 3 (deliberately orphan a tenant row in db_test, run --auto-fix, confirm reconciliation) since this path has never been observed to succeed.

evidence_file: N/A -- reproduced directly via `python tools/verify_schema_baseline.py --check-tenants --auto-fix` against db_test during WF03-gh454-20260806; the 2 orphaned rows in that run were cleaned up directly via SQL (DELETE FROM public.tenant WHERE id IN (...)) since the tool's own auto-fix path is broken. Root cause re-confirmed independently via direct source read + git history during WF03-gh458-20260806 (this run).
resolution: Fixed in tools/verify_schema_baseline.py on branch feature/WF03-gh458-20260806. Added resolve_reconcile_migration(), which resolves the reconcile migration dynamically by glob ('*_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql') under migrations_dir instead of a hardcoded literal filename, so the lookup survives future renumbering without requiring another source edit. Replaced the unbounded recursive `return main()` retry with a bounded loop guarded by MAX_AUTO_FIX_ATTEMPTS = 2 (one initial check plus at most one post-auto-fix recheck), and changed auto_fix() to return a bool/status so the caller can distinguish 'fix applied, recheck once' from 'fix failed, stop immediately' instead of always re-invoking main() on any failure. Verified via two independent manual repros against a deliberately-orphaned public.tenant row on db_test: BACKEND-DEV Step 3 (initial fix verification) and TEST-RUNNER Step 5 (independent re-verification with a freshly-inserted orphaned row, UUID f7a3fa1f-03ba-444c-b4cc-c995e750777f). Both confirmed --auto-fix correctly resolves and applies GBL-133_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql dynamically, exactly 2 bounded check attempts (not unbounded recursion), zero GBL-105 references remaining anywhere in source or runtime output, and no connection leak (pg_stat_activity count for bpm_test unchanged before/after, 1 -> 1).
prevention: This is the third confirmed instance of the same anti-pattern class: a hardcoded exact migration filename silently desyncing after a rename, with no compile-time signal (ISS-0088/GH#337 was the first; a second recurrence was fixed incidentally during ISS-0144/GH#454's cleanup, GBL-077->GBL-116). The general prevention: wherever a migration or artefact filename embeds a mutable numeric ID (the GBL-NNN prefix, which is subject to renumbering when siblings are inserted/reordered) alongside a stable descriptive suffix (e.g. '_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql'), any code that needs to locate that file at runtime should resolve it by glob/pattern match on the stable suffix rather than hardcoding the full filename including the numeric prefix. Reserve literal filename references for contexts where the exact name is inherently part of the contract (e.g. a migration's own entry in schema_migrations). Related: ISS-0088 (GH#337), the GBL-077->GBL-116 fix folded into ISS-0144 (GH#454).
